findings.claim: The V0 brief's founding premise is false: RETINA M2 is not orphaned. It landed 2026-07-17 and shipped as v5.29.0.
findings.anchor: git patch-id --stable: f3be38c -> d8d5efce6b64144101c81070808bb2003b66a9b3; 1d160a9 -> d8d5efce6b64144101c81070808bb2003b66a9b3. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 1d160a9 master` -> true. `git tag --list v5.29*` -> v5.29.0. b538a31 'release: v5.29.0 — RETINA T1: the scoped-delta proof engine is live'. 0a740e6 'chore(flywheel): RETINA.M2 -> merged'.
findings.root_cause: harness/notes/receipts/F1.json:226 recorded 'present on NO other branch'. That test was `git branch --contains <SHA>`, which is correct for the SHA and WRONG for the question. f3be38c is the pre-rebase copy that lived in a workflow worktree; 1d160a9 is the rebased copy that landed. Different SHA, identical patch. SHA-containment answered a narrower question than the one being asked, and the receipt inherited the narrower answer.
findings.was_F1_wrong_at_the_time: YES — not merely stale. 1d160a9 is an ancestor of repair/f1-integrate, F1's OWN branch, whose tip a64033d is dated 2026-07-26. The work was in F1's tree while F1 declared it existed nowhere.
findings.class: This is the R91 class exactly: a check that could not see the composition it was asked about. R91 was two legs rewriting one function invisibly to each other; F1 is one leg testing SHA identity when patch identity was the question.

The four orchestrator tests cover contained-change, leaked-change, no-baseline and no-ID-AOV. The promised fifth case is unpinned.
findings.failure_scenario: The M3 worker drains an outbox and hands T1 a baseline from a previous render at a different resolution — a res change mid-session, a proxy frame, a partially-written EXR. Instead of an inconclusive verdict the worker loop takes an unhandled exception and dies. That is the SAME failure mode the crucible caught in T0 and fixed in 3cc392f ('would kill the M3 worker loop draining a corrupted on-disk manifest'). The class was fixed in T0 and left live in T1.
findings.probe: <scratchpad>/t1_honesty2.py + t1_trace.py under C:/Python314/python.exe with cv2 4.12.0; 9 orchestrator cases driven, 3 crashed, tracebacks captured to the retina-side frame.

The M2 crucible deposited RETINA.M3-worker-hardening (0a740e6, still status=candidate / ratified=false on HEAD) with FOUR bounded findings: JSONL verdict atomicity vs PIPE_BUF, a T0 path-containment guard, resolve_profile leaf-only merge semantics, and the unverified OIIO ingest leg. findings.anchor: tests/test_retina_t1.py:25-28 sets pytestmark = skipif(not (_HAS_CV2 and _HAS_NUMPY)); the test then asserts `t1.pixels_available() is True`. findings.claim: A resolved qc profile does not record WHICH profile produced it.
findings.anchor: retina/qc_profiles.py:79-91 resolve_profile returns a flat dict with no provenance key; retina/t1.py:450-474 reads values out of it into checks. An unknown renderer silently inherits [default] (pinned as correct by tests/test_retina_t1_schema.py:168-174).
findings.assessment: NOT a Law 3 violation — the threshold VALUES ride on every check (leak_px/eps, val/min), so a reader can always see what was asserted against. What a reader cannot see is whether those came from [default] or from a renderer-specific table. Cheap to add, worth adding before QC gating goes live, not worth blocking anything now.
findings.relation_to_existing_queue: ADJACENT to, not a duplicate of, RETINA.M3-worker-hardening item (3) — that item is about resolve_profile ignoring INTERMEDIATE tables (confirmed: retina/qc_profiles.py:81-86 returns [default] the moment any level misses, so a [renderer.policy] table with no [.tier] leaf contributes nothing). findings.claim: assess_frame FAILS a physically ordinary scene-linear render. The pixels are un-transformed HDR; the thresholds are a 0..1 display-referred window. The frame-health tier is a false-positive machine as shipped.
findings.the_seam: retina/ingest.py:158-160 commits to returning UN-transformed scene-linear pixels ('already linear (lin_rec709)'), deliberately and correctly. retina/t1.py:454-459 then tests those unbounded HDR values against low=black_threshold=0.001 / high=blown_threshold=0.999 from retina/qc_profiles.toml:38-39. On a linear plane, 'above 0.999' does not mean 'clipped' — it means 'brighter than diffuse white', which is every window, sky, specular and practical light in the frame.
findings.probe: 256x256 scene-linear frame at 0.18 diffuse grey with 20% of the frame at 4.0 linear, run through the SHIPPED [default] profile. Producer: <scratchpad>/critic_verify.py under C:/Python314/python.exe, cv2 4.12.0, numpy 2.2.6.
findings.result: clip_percent pass=False 'clip=0.1992 > ratio=0.05'; assess_frame VERDICT = 'fail'. Sole-sourced from clip_percent — a red, not an inconclusive.
findings.why_it_matters_here: harness/SYNAPSE_RETINA_VERIFY.md:44-62 lists five ways this instrument lies and demands they be measured before the thing they guard is built. This is a sixth, and it is not a measurement error — it is a units mismatch between two files that are each internally consistent. V2 is the declared gate; a gate whose frame-health tier reds a correct render cannot certify anything.
findings.the_fix_is_NOT_loosening_clip_ratio: retina/qc_profiles.toml:9-12 states Commandment 7 for thresholds explicitly: 'A threshold is a test assertion. It is NEVER loosened to green a verdict.' Raising clip_ratio would be exactly that. The defect is that blown_threshold is display-referred while the plane is scene-referred; the honest repairs are to define the clip test against the EXR's actual value range, or to run it on a display-transformed proxy (which ingest.py:26-29 already scopes to M5), or to declare the metric inconclusive on un-normalised linear data.
findings.provenance: Surfaced by the completeness critic as a cross-file seam no per-file reader could see; INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED by this orchestrator before being recorded.

findings.claim: The zero-cv2 host boundary — blueprint P5, 'The eye never destabilizes the hand' — is enforced by a check that cannot fail in the way that matters. It is textual, not transitive, and M2 is the commit that created the hazard it is blind to.
the_mechanism: tests/test_retina_boundary.py:38-55 scans python/synapse, shared/, houdini/ and mcp_server.py with the regex ^\s*(?:import\s+cv2\b|from\s+cv2\b), and DELIBERATELY excludes retina/ (:25, :36-37).

python/synapse/panel/render_receipt.py:42-53 runs INSIDE the Houdini process, does `from retina.t0 import check_manifest_against_disk`, and on ImportError inserts the REPO ROOT at sys.path[0] and retries. The host itself puts the retina package on its own import path.
M2 is the commit that put `import cv2` (retina/t1.py:63) into that package.
findings.probe: python -c 'import retina.t0' -> cv2 in sys.modules: False. Then 'import retina.t1' -> cv2 in sys.modules: True (4.12.0). Same process.
findings.status_today: The property HOLDS. retina/__init__.py imports only two constants and retina/t0.py reaches only .events, so the host path never touches t1. Nothing is broken right now.
findings.status_tomorrow: It holds by convention, not by construction. One line — `from .t1 import ...` added to retina/__init__.py or retina/t0.py — loads OpenCV into Houdini's process, and test_host_process_has_no_cv2_imports stays GREEN, because the literal string never appears in a scanned file. Law 1: state the condition under which the check fails. It fails on a literal import in four named paths. It cannot fail on transitive import through a package the host puts on sys.path itself.
findings.proportionality: Recorded as major, not showstopper, because nothing is currently violated and the fix is small (assert on sys.modules after importing the host entry point, or scan the transitive closure). But it is the exact shape of Law 1's four cited instances: a check reporting healthy, continuously, while proving less than it claims.

findings.claim: Metric 2 (black_blown_frame) is strictly dominated by metric 3 (clip_percent) and can never be the sole red at any ratified tolerance.
findings.anchor: retina/t1.py:448-459 feeds BOTH metrics the same low/high thresholds. retina/qc_profiles.toml:40-41 sets black_ratio=0.95 and clip_ratio=0.05, so black_blown needs 19x the pixel population clip_percent needs. Neither override table (:46-52) touches either ratio, so this holds for all three shipped profiles.
findings.observed: On the F9 probe frame: clip pass=False while black_blown pass=True — the dominance made visible.
findings.assessment: Not a correctness bug; a redundancy that costs a metric slot and inflates the apparent breadth of the seven-metric kit. Worth knowing before the kit's coverage is cited as evidence.

findings.claim: Invoked as the bare `pytest` console script, the entire M2 test surface is a COLLECTION ERROR, not a skip.

So `from retina import ...` at tests/test_retina_t1_schema.py:22 resolves ONLY because `python -m pytest` injects CWD.

findings.claim: retina/setup_venv.ps1's failure handler cannot fire, so a failed pip install reports success — a Law 3 violation.
findings.anchor: retina/setup_venv.ps1:39-50 wraps `& $vpy -m pip install -r $reqs` in try/catch and relies on $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' (:18) to turn a native-command failure into a terminating error. It does not. $LASTEXITCODE is never checked anywhere in the file.
findings.probe: powershell -NoProfile -Command "$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'; try { & cmd.exe /c 'exit 1'; 'FELL-THROUGH' } catch { 'CATCH FIRED' }" -> FELL-THROUGH, LASTEXITCODE=1, PSVersion=5.1.26100.8894.
findings.consequence: Control falls through to setup_venv.ps1:52-55, which prints 'RETINA worker venv ready: <path>' and exits 0 over an empty or half-populated venv. setup_venv.ps1:1-2 calls itself the 'Windows twin of setup_venv.py'; the Python twin does NOT share the defect (subprocess.check_call raises, setup_venv.py:69-78). They diverge on the one behaviour that matters.
findings.compounds_F3: F3 says the venv is not created. F13 says that on Windows, the failure to create it is reported as success. That is worse than the gap.

findings.claim: requirements.txt's graceful-degradation promise is unreachable, and both scripts misattribute the failure.
findings.anchor: retina/requirements.txt:33-37 states that where no OIIO wheel resolves 'the worker still runs every cv2 T1 metric ... only the EXR file-read leg is OIIO-owed on that platform.' But OpenImageIO==3.1.15.0 (:40) is a hard pin in the same file as opencv-python-headless==5.0.0.93 (:28); pip resolves the whole set before installing, so an unresolvable OIIO pin aborts the entire install and cv2 is not installed either. You get an empty venv, not a cv2-only one.
findings.compounds: Both failure handlers (setup_venv.py:71-77, setup_venv.ps1:43-48) attribute ANY resolution failure to OpenCV — pointing the operator at the pin that resolved. And requirements.txt:14-17 ('the abi3 wheel spans cp37+ ... so ANY local interpreter can seed the venv') is true of the OpenCV line but false of the file, since the only OIIO wheel it names is cp314 while the seeding path it recommends is cp313.
findings.not_probed: Marked VERIFIED-STATIC, not RUNTIME: confirming pip's abort behaviour would require a network install, which is outside a read-only verdict leg's remit. The claim rests on pip's documented resolve-then-install order and the file's own text.

findings.claim: The M2 test surface is broad but shallow: mutation testing shows the suite stays green while load-bearing implementations are replaced by stubs. Twelve such gaps survived adversarial verification.
findings.method: 51 candidate defects were raised by six independent per-file readers and each was then attacked by a separate verifier instructed to REFUTE it and to default to refuted when uncertain. 39 were refuted. 12 survived. The survivors are listed below with their anchors; all were established by MUTATION (break the implementation, observe the suite) rather than by reading.
survivors: M2T-03 (major) tests/test_retina_t1.py:248 — project_bbox: REMOVING THE Y-FLIP at retina/t1.py:404 leaves the test passing. The y-flip is the mechanism behind the 'one top-down orientation' claim (retina/ingest.py:30-33). Switching the row-vector multiply at :396 to column-vector also passes. Two of the test's four assertions merely restate the clamp.

M2T-04 (major) tests/test_retina_t1.py:116 — test_ssim_identical_is_one holds by algebraic symmetry, not by implementation: with x==y the numerator and denominator are the identical expression, so it returns 1.0 even with cv2.GaussianBlur stubbed to return zeros. Combined with the other two SSIM tests, the SSIM implementation has NO numerical ground truth anywhere in the repo.
M2T-01 (minor) tests/test_retina_t1.py:173 — ssim_outside, half of the scoped-delta proof, can be replaced by an unconditional green and all 22 T1 tests still pass.

M2T-10 (minor) tests/test_retina_t1.py:142 — id_matte: a mutant computing (ids != 0) and IGNORING target_id is byte-identical on every fixture; forcing dilation=0 also passes. All 8 id_plane call sites use a single region with target_id 7.

M2T-11 (minor) tests/test_retina_t1.py:130 — change_mask: forcing morph_radius=0 leaves 22/22 passing. The fixture is a clean rectangle on a noise-free gradient, so there is no speckle to open and no pinhole to close.

M2T-06 (minor) tests/test_retina_ingest.py:87 — 'header locates the ID subimage (no hardcoded index)' is unverified: monkeypatching find_id_subimage to `lambda p: 1` leaves all runnable ingest tests passing, because every fixture writes the ID part at index 1.

M2T-05 (minor) tests/test_retina_ingest.py:68 — the 'topdown' test cannot detect a vertical flip: gradient_plane (img_synth.py:41-43) tiles one row down the frame, so it EQUALS its own vertical flip, and the only orientation assertion compares left-vs-right within row 0.

M2T-02 (minor) tests/test_retina_t1.py:263 — the tautological test (this leg's F4, found independently). Additionally: T1Unavailable is asserted in no test anywhere, despite the docstring claiming it is covered.

M2T-15 (note) tests/test_retina_t1.py:58 — the inf half of nan_inf_census has no negative control: inf_count is only ever asserted ==0, img_synth has inject_nan but no inject_inf, so np.isinf at retina/t1.py:132 is never proven to fire. A typo replacing it with np.isnan ships green. (The clip half of this finding was refuted.)
D3 (minor) retina/ingest.py:143 — see the OIIO note below.
D4 (minor) retina/setup_venv.py:57 — the venv finding, independently reached; see F3.
findings.proportionality: This is NOT a claim that T1 is wrong. This orchestrator drove the scoped-delta primitive behaviourally and it discriminates correctly (leak_px 0 vs 60 against eps=32). It is a claim that the SUITE would not tell you if it stopped discriminating. Every survivor is a Law 1 instance: a check that reports healthy while proving less than its name implies.
findings.refuted_for_balance: 39 of 51 candidates did NOT survive, including every claim that the envelope/roll-up/honesty pins are weak, the entire qc_profiles key-space attack except RQC-4, and 5 of 6 venv claims. The schema/governance layer (tests/test_retina_t1_schema.py) held under attack.

findings.claim: resolve_profile's docstring says the merge 'only ever narrows or restates tolerances ... it never invents or loosens one' — and the shipped TOML's own override table loosens both knobs it touches.
findings.anchor: retina/qc_profiles.py:76-78 (the claim) vs retina/qc_profiles.toml:46-48, [karma_xpu.denoised.low]: ssim_min 0.995 -> 0.990 (a LOWER structural-similarity floor is easier to pass) and diff_threshold 0.02 -> 0.03 (a LARGER abs-diff floor means fewer pixels count as changed). Both moves are permissive.
findings.fairness: The loosening is well-reasoned and stated in the config — qc_profiles.toml:44-45 explains that XPU denoiser smear and GPU noise widen the floor, and comparing denoised-vs-denoised like-for-like is correct practice. The defect is the DOCSTRING, which asserts a property the ratified data contradicts. Under Commandment 7 the distinction matters: a tolerance widened by ratified config is legitimate; the docstring claims the loader structurally cannot do it, which would make an unratified widening invisible rather than impossible.
findings.relation: Adjacent to F6 (no provenance recorded) and to the already-queued RETINA.M3-worker-hardening item (3) (intermediate tables ignored). Three separate true statements about one 27-line function.

verdict.why: Not because the work is bad — the work is good and is ALREADY LANDED. Reject because (a) `git diff HEAD <merge-tree>` is empty, so merging accomplishes literally nothing, and (b) the branch's retina/t0.py is the PRE-crucible-fix version; any resolution that took its side would revert 3cc392f, a shipped showstopper fix. There is no state of the world in which merging this branch is an improvement.
verdict.on_the_WORK_M2_contains: ALREADY LANDED — and, on the evidence gathered here, soundly. Byte-identical T0 refactor proved at the byte level across 18 cases including error paths. Schema-siblinghood is structural and test-pinned. The scoped-delta primitive discriminates correctly (leak_px=0 on a contained change, 60 on a leaked one, against eps=32). Missing-input paths are honestly inconclusive. Zero hou, zero host-side cv2, base-module cv2 only. The OIIO version-skew risk was probed and refuted.
verdict.on_what_HEAD_still_needs: LAND WITH NAMED FIXES applies not to the branch but to the CURRENT tree. NAMED FIXES, in priority order: F9 (assess_frame reds a physically ordinary scene-linear render — display-referred thresholds on scene-linear pixels; blocks V2, which is the declared gate), F2 (shape-mismatch crashes in three T1 orchestrator paths, contradicting an explicit docstring promise — the same class the crucible already fixed in T0), F10 (the zero-cv2 host boundary is textual, not transitive, and M2 created the hazard it is blind to), F3+F13+F14 (the worker venv is uncreated, its documented hython seed path is broken, and on Windows that failure reports SUCCESS), F15 (twelve mutation-proven coverage gaps — the suite would not tell you if T1 stopped discriminating). None of these blocks V1, which is a read-only capture probe.
verdict.revised_confidence_note: The verdict on the WORK is unchanged by the findings above and should not be read as softened. The scoped-delta primitive — the one sentence this harness exists to produce — was driven behaviourally and discriminates correctly. What the findings establish is that the surrounding instrument is less measured than its documentation implies: three governing sentences (the shape-mismatch promise, the 'never loosens' promise, the P5 boundary) assert properties the code does not currently hold, and the test surface would not report it. That is a hardening bill on a sound core, not a rebuild.
verdict.on_the_branch_ref_itself: KEEP the ref, do not delete it in this leg. Law 4: classify before you delete, and deletion is a separate human act. It is now CLASSIFIED — superseded duplicate of 1d160a9, patch-id d8d5efce, retained at zero cost. Recommend renaming or annotating it so the next reader does not re-open this question; that is a human call, not an agent's.

for_ruling.question: F1's 'present on NO other branch' was produced by `git branch --contains <SHA>` and was false when written. Should branch-orphan classification require a patch-id check?
for_ruling.why_it_is_a_ruling: It is a value judgement about how much verification a housekeeping step owes, not a fact provable from the tree. The cost is one `git patch-id --stable` per candidate branch; the benefit is that a rebased-then-landed commit stops reading as orphaned work.
for_ruling.proposed: Any receipt claiming a branch carries unique work must cite BOTH `git branch --contains <sha>` AND `git patch-id --stable` matched against the tips it claims are missing it. This is a check that can fail today — it would have failed on F1.json:226 — which is the Law 1 bar.
for_ruling.relation: Direct descendant of R91 (a check answering a narrower question than the one asked) and R92 (collisions invisible until integration).

for_ruling.question: F2: should the T1 shape-mismatch fix be its own leg, or folded into V2?
for_ruling.why_it_is_a_ruling: A defensible-options call. It is a real defect with a broken docstring promise, but V2 (noise floor + ID stability) is the declared gate and will exercise exactly these orchestrators with real renders — arguably the right place to find and fix it under load. Against that: shipping V2 on a T1 that crashes on a res change means the gate's own instrument can die mid-measurement.
for_ruling.recommendation: Fold into V2's opening move rather than a standalone leg — V2 is where mismatched-shape inputs actually arise, and the fix is small (a shape guard at the top of both orchestrators returning the inconclusive checks the docstring already promises), but it must land BEFORE V2's measurements are trusted, not after.
for_ruling.not_decided_here: Article I — an agent may not decide what a leg's scope should be.

for_ruling.question: F3: who creates the worker venv, and with which interpreter?
for_ruling.why_it_is_a_ruling: Two defensible options with different costs. (a) System python 3.14.2 seed — works today, gets both pinned wheels, but is a third interpreter in a repo that already juggles hython 3.13.10 and system 3.14.2. (b) Fix the hython seed path — keeps the worker on the DCC's interpreter and inherits Houdini's OIIO, but requires solving ensurepip-103 and the missing bin/python.exe, and pyvenv.cfg would need --system-site-packages which is a different isolation posture than the blueprint's 'host-ABI-independent by construction'.
for_ruling.evidence_for_the_decision: Option (a) is VERIFIED-RUNTIME working on this machine. Option (b) is VERIFIED-RUNTIME broken on this machine. That does not decide it — (b) may be worth fixing — but the asymmetry is real and measured.
for_ruling.blocking: V4 explicitly ('cv2 mask kit ... in the worker venv'). NOT blocking V1 (read-only capture probe) or V2 (noise floor, which needs renders and hython, not cv2).

for_ruling.question: F9: the frame-health tier reds a correct scene-linear render. Is V2 gated on fixing it, and which repair?
for_ruling.why_it_is_a_ruling: Three defensible repairs with different costs, and the choice sets a convention the whole tier ladder inherits. (a) Define the clip test against the EXR's actual value range rather than a fixed 0..1 window — keeps the metric on linear data, but 'clipped' becomes relative and needs its own definition. (b) Run clip/black-blown on a display-transformed proxy — matches how a human judges exposure, but ingest.py:26-29 scopes the display proxy to M5, so this pulls M5 work forward. (c) Return inconclusive on un-normalised linear data — honest, cheap, and consistent with §7, but silences two of the seven metrics until (a) or (b) lands.
for_ruling.what_is_NOT_a_defensible_option: Raising clip_ratio. retina/qc_profiles.toml:9-12 forbids it in the file's own words, and it would convert a units bug into a tuned tolerance — the exact move Commandment 7 exists to stop.
for_ruling.recommendation: (c) now, as a one-line honesty guard that unblocks V2 immediately, with (a) or (b) ruled separately. for_ruling.question: F10: should the zero-cv2 host boundary be enforced by reachability rather than by regex?
for_ruling.why_it_is_a_ruling: It is a cost/benefit call on a check that is not currently failing. Nothing is violated today. The cheap version is one assertion — import the host entry point in a subprocess and assert 'cv2' not in sys.modules — which would fail the moment retina/__init__.py or t0.py reaches t1. The thorough version walks the transitive import closure of the host surfaces and is more work than the risk currently justifies.
for_ruling.recommendation: The cheap version. It is a check that can fail, it costs one test, and it converts P5 from a convention into a mechanism. Note this is the SAME shape as the Article IV principle that enforcement belongs in the definition rather than the instruction.

drift.correction: A fan-out that hands one agent the aggregate of the others must either pass the payload whole or state the truncation IN the prompt so the critic knows what it is missing. Silent slicing produces an agent that cannot know what it did not see.
